news.title: Synthetic benchmark increase: funding costs, deposit income and investment decisions in 2027
news.text: SYNTHETIC TEST PUBLICATION, entirely invented. The fictional FixtureBench-E benchmark rises from 12 percent to 14 percent effective 1 January 2027 and stays at 14 percent for 2027 in this synthetic scenario. Floating-rate business loans explicitly indexed to FixtureBench-E with immediate reset and unchanged principal would face a 2 percentage point rate increase; fixed-rate contracts do not automatically reprice. At RUB 1000000 principal maintained for 365 days on an ACT/365 basis and without floors, caps or offsets, the conditional incremental annual interest would be RUB 20000. This arithmetic example is not a claim about any company. New borrowing and refinancing may become more costly, firms may postpone debt-financed investment or reassess working-capital needs, while eligible floating-rate deposits may earn more. Actual contracts, index identity, reset dates, balances, hedges, liquidity needs and deposits must be verified from each company original; preserve unknown if not documented. These are conditional causal mechanisms, not asserted company forecasts or real bank guidance.
